sights.w: Bishan's public sports hub, run by Sport Singapore's ActiveSG, built around a stadium (opened 1998) with a professional running track that is the main home ground of Singapore Premier League club Lion City Sailors (formerly Home United). The wider centre adds a sports hall, clubhouse courts, swimming pool and a YouthCreates skate spot beside Bishan-AMK Park.
sights.k: Public sessions daily; stadium track free when open

sights.n: Old Upper Thomson Road (former Grand Prix circuit)
sights.w: The quiet, tree-lined loop on Bishan's northern doorstep that was Singapore's most notorious motor-racing venue — the ~4.9km Thomson Road street circuit hosted the Singapore Grand Prix from 1961 to 1973, with legendary corners named Devil's Bend, The Snakes and Murder Mile. Once lined with kampongs, parts of the old route now thread Thomson Nature Park and skirt Lower Peirce.
sights.k: Public road / park connector, open daily, free

sights.address: Junction of Sin Ming Drive & Sin Ming Avenue, Sin Ming, Singapore
sights.w: A Buddhist temple at the Sin Ming Drive / Sin Ming Avenue junction that doubles as a crematorium — one of only two privately run cremation facilities in Singapore, the other being at nearby Kong Meng San Phor Kark See. A quiet Sin Ming heritage landmark documented in the National Heritage Board's Roots collection.
